issues.text: L2 resolved as the task said: the two fixed messages are exact; the place of a failure is carried by the collector (problems.add(place, [message])), so these two fail at the end of the test, with the place in '(N x; e.g. place)'. All other messages are assertions with the place in the text; the message templates of design 9.2 for LD-3 rows 1-5 are not word for word (they are not fixed by the requirement): mine read '<where>: <what>' with where = 'how.html <lang> <scheme>'.

Choices beyond the design text, all within its criteria: row 1 checks every question screen, not only the last; row 15 at >= 1000 px asserts the side area is right of the receipt block with equal tops (|d| <= 0.5 px), at <= 1000 px the strict order of tops (sum, side, answers, lists on a recommended result; sum, lists, side, answers on no match), both read from the measured F13; the block element on a retry is checked to be the same node (design 5 row 4: 'the block is not rebuilt'); LD-3/LD-9 also assert every part of the block and each mark is visible; TX-10 adds 11 damaged copies of the page and TX-9 adds cases by class of input so each is no blind rule. The count k of the receipt is computed from the pass's answers (given = 1, skipped = 0.5), the own oracle of criterion 5.

The permission classifier refused one command of mine: loading the scratch copy of texts.test.js with a stub of node:test and calling TX-4, TX-9 and TX-10 (it counts as running tests, which the owner's rule forbids on this PC). I did not repeat it or work around it. TX-4's added rows (the exact values, the file scan, the order_ check) were therefore not executed at all on this PC; they were checked by reading, by the literals check against the module and the requirement, and by grep (no file under app/public or app/test holds the removed key's name). TX-9 and TX-10 helper logic was executed through function cut-outs as described; the bodies of TX-9 and TX-10 (the loops and the damaged-copy table) were not.

Mutants M12, M47, M48, M52, M26 and the module-level ones are not run here (they need larger edits of demo.js or of the texts module that I did not express safely as one-line edits); they are in mutants_for_ci with the test that must turn red. M44's first version used an inline style and was caught only by the CSP record (a different guard); the replaced version is red by the first-screen assertion.
The product code was not changed; no test needed an edit of it. No Q8/Q11/R3 test (not touched, reasons in the table).
